title: NIST AI RMF Trustworthy AI Characteristics
description: The seven characteristics of trustworthy AI as defined in the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. All characteristics are interconnected — improving one may tension with another (e.g., transparency vs. security). Organizations should document trade-off decisions.

title: NIST AI RMF Core Functions Overview

function_descriptions.GOVERN: Cross-cutting function: sets organizational context, culture, and accountability structures for AI risk management. Underpins the other three functions.
function_descriptions.MAP: Establishes context, identifies risk sources, and categorizes AI risks before measurement and management.
function_descriptions.MEASURE: Analyzes and evaluates AI risks and trustworthiness using quantitative and qualitative methods (TEVV activities).
function_descriptions.MANAGE: Prioritizes and addresses AI risks, implements controls, documents residual risks, and drives continuous improvement.

description: The NIST AI RMF is organized around four core functions that together provide a comprehensive lifecycle approach to AI risk management. GOVERN is foundational; MAP-MEASURE-MANAGE form an iterative risk management loop.

title: NIST AI RMF Profiles
description: A Profile is a selection of GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE subcategories that an organization prioritizes based on their risk context. Organizations create a Current Profile (as-is state) and a Target Profile (desired state) to guide improvement. Sector-specific profiles (e.g., financial services, healthcare) extend the core framework.

title: NIST AI RMF Playbook
description: The NIST AI RMF Playbook (NIST AI 600-1 companion) provides suggested actions for each subcategory of the AI RMF, organized by function. It is a voluntary, non-prescriptive resource. Organizations select relevant actions based on their context, maturity, and risk tolerance.
source: NIST AI RMF Playbook (NIST AI 100-1 companion)

title: NIST AI RMF Generative AI Supplement (NIST AI 600-1)
description: NIST AI 600-1 (2024) supplements the AI RMF for generative AI systems, including LLMs. It introduces 12 unique risks for GenAI: CBRN information, confabulation (hallucination), data privacy, data provenance, harmful bias, homogenization, human-AI configuration, information integrity, information security, intellectual property, obscene/abusive/violent content, and value chain/supply chain risks.
